biological_interpretation: ERRalpha and PGC-1beta participate in a susceptible-neuron mitochondrial transcriptional axis that is not interchangeable with PGC-1alpha or broad PPAR/RXR receptor loss.
caveats: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had the highest perturbed-cell count, although other high-count classes still lacked FDR hits.
Absence of target-transcript depletion does not exclude guide activity at protein or isoform levels, but the measured RNA evidence is weak.
The genome-wide correlation was small, so the comparison is restricted-signature and hypothesis-generating.
Both coactivator perturbations showed weak measured on-target mRNA effects, so divergence could reflect perturbation quality rather than true paralog-specific biology.
All compared perturbations had weak target-transcript depletion, so lack of correlation could reflect perturbation strength as well as biology.

Exact log2 fold changes, scores, p-values, and FDRs in exact_de_rows were re-read from the Wilcoxon Parquet; the graph and cluster summaries were used only to nominate the target/readout combinations.
exact_observed_result: Esrra loss produced a robust 151 TH-specific decrease of TCA, pyruvate, OXPHOS-linked, membrane, axon-adhesion, and synaptic transcripts; Ppargc1b perturbation exposed a selective mitochondrial signal with Atp5b FDR-supported in 155 MB Glut and recurrent decreases in Idh3b, Uqcrc1, Dlst, Atp5j, Slc25a3, and Ndufa10; Esrra was the closest positive Ppargc1b neighbor in 151 TH, while Ppargc1a and PPAR receptors did not phenocopy Ppargc1b. Parquet-verified leading rows: Esrra->Gas6 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.556, FDR 1.56e-09; Esrra->Bcan in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.937, FDR 2.38e-06; Esrra->Nceh1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.376, FDR 8.11e-06; Esrra->Nsg2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC 0.379, FDR 7.45e-05; Esrra->Mdh1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.25, FDR 1.53e-04; Esrra->Atp1b1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.209, FDR 1.53e-04.

prior_expectation.summary: References were retained only when they were linked to one of the resolved source findings.

finding_summaries.summary: Esrra has a single robust FDR-significant response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: The perturbation cannot be interpreted as a pan-neuronal ESRRA program; downstream analysis should focus on the one class with both target mRNA depletion and corrected effects.

finding_summaries.summary: Most assayed Ppargc1b perturbations were transcriptionally weak: target RNA was never FDR-significantly reduced and only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.05 across the full Ppargc1b slice.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: The negative result prevents overcalling the many nominal tails as complete PGC-1beta loss of function and makes cell-count and target-engagement caveats first-order biological constraints.

finding_summaries.summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Esrra was the closest positive Ppargc1b signature neighbor and co-depleted metabolic genes including Idh3b, Uqcrc1, Mdh1, and Dlst.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: The dataset gives an exploratory in situ echo of the known PGC-1beta-ERR connection in the same cell type in which Ppargc1b showed its strongest sub-FDR TCA/OXPHOS tail.

finding_summaries.summary: Ppargc1a and Ppargc1b signatures were nearly uncorrelated, and the single Ppargc1b Atp5b hit was not reproduced by Ppargc1a.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: PGC-1 coactivator paralogs should be considered separately in this dataset; the Ppargc1b result does not rescue or proxy for the failed Ppargc1a perturbation.

finding_summaries.summary: Ppargc1b was not transcriptomically interchangeable with Ppargc1a or the assayed PPAR receptors in the main responder classes.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: Even though PPARGC1B is a PGC-1-family PPAR coactivator, the neuronal Ppargc1b knockdown signature appears more selective than a generic PPAR-family perturbation signature.

resolved_evidence.description: On-target Esrra transcript depletion in the only cell class with an FDR-significant Esrra response.
resolved_evidence.statistics: 275 perturbed cells versus 23679 controls; Esrra Wilcoxon score -5.334, logFC -0.4806, p=9.61e-08, FDR=2.07e-04.

resolved_evidence.description: Size, direction, and leading genes of the Esrra response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
resolved_evidence.statistics: 57 genes at FDR<0.05 including Esrra; 56 downstream genes; 41/57 FDR rows lower; 112 genes with raw p<0.001. Gas6 score -7.454 logFC -0.5559 FDR=1.56e-09; Bcan score -6.312 logFC -0.9374 FDR=2.38e-06; Nceh1 score -6.054 logFC -0.3757 FDR=8.11e-06; Nsg2 score 5.637 logFC 0.3786 FDR=7.45e-05.

resolved_evidence.description: Cell-type distribution of multiple-testing-corrected Esrra responses.
resolved_evidence.statistics: 23 cell classes tested; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had 57 FDR<0.05 rows, while the other 22 classes each had 0 FDR<0.05 rows. Perturbed-cell counts ranged from 21 to 275 and matched controls from 2019 to 23679.

resolved_evidence.description: Direct target-transcript rows for the Ppargc1b perturbation show weak, non-FDR-significant RNA depletion wherever Ppargc1b was measured.
resolved_evidence.statistics: 21 measured cell types; 30-170 perturbed cells per cell type, median 55; on-target Ppargc1b logFC ranged from -0.576 to +0.135; minimum nominal p=0.008744; pvals_adj=1.0 for all 21 target-transcript rows; 3/21 rows were nominally negative at p<0.05.

resolved_evidence.description: The Ppargc1b perturbation produced a very sparse FDR-significant response despite nominal tails in every assayed cell type.
resolved_evidence.statistics: 355046 gene-by-cell-type Ppargc1b tests across 21 cell types yielded 1 FDR<0.05 row; 20/21 cell types had zero FDR<0.05 genes. Per-cell-type nominal p<0.05 counts ranged from 264 to 455 among approximately 16428-17443 tested genes.

resolved_evidence.description: A restricted-signature comparison links the Ppargc1b nominal metabolic tail to a stronger Esrra perturbation in the same cell type.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Within 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Esrra was the top positive Ppargc1b score-signature neighbor among 2045 other perturbations, Pearson r=0.0946; 30 genes had score<-2 under both Ppargc1b and Esrra. Shared negative examples: Idh3b, Ppargc1b logFC -0.340/FDR 0.225 and Esrra logFC -0.250/FDR 0.0288; Uqcrc1, -0.226/0.282 and -0.197/0.0725; Mdh1, -0.147/1.0 and -0.250/1.53e-4; Dlst, -0.241/1.0 and -0.168/0.998.

resolved_evidence.description: Paralog signature correlations were near zero across all matched cell classes.
resolved_evidence.statistics: 21 Ppargc1a-matched cell classes; Ppargc1a versus Ppargc1b score-vector Pearson correlations ranged from -0.044 to 0.130, and Spearman correlations ranged from -0.031 to 0.111.

resolved_evidence.description: Ppargc1b gave only one corrected hit and it was not reproduced by Ppargc1a in the same cell class.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Across 355046 Ppargc1b rows in 21 classes, only Atp5b in 155 MB Glut was FDR-significant: 124 perturbed cells versus 20353 controls, Atp5b logFC -0.515, p=4.32e-7, FDR=0.00754. In the same 155 MB Glut class under Ppargc1a perturbation, Atp5b logFC was -0.165, p=0.152, FDR=1.0.

resolved_evidence.description: Perturbations of the PGC-1 paralog and assayed PPAR nuclear receptors did not reproduce the Ppargc1b mitochondrial signature in the strongest Ppargc1b contexts.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Score correlations with Ppargc1b were near zero for Ppara/Ppard/Pparg in the two main responder classes: in 155 MB Glut, r=0.013/0.022/-0.018; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, r=0.0086/-0.017/0.0081. Ppargc1a correlations were also weak, r=0.033 in 155 MB Glut and r=0.0636 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. The Ppara, Ppard, and Pparg perturbations did not nominally reduce Atp5b or Idh3b in 155 MB Glut.

title: Esrra and Ppargc1b perturbations reveal separable mitochondrial programs in thalamic and midbrain neurons
